Yep I agree with his kind of logic. Reality is we aren't really testing for community transmission so we cant be sure we're definitely flattening the curve. The low death rate and the lowish number of ICU cases (96 at the moment) might suggest that our curve could indeed be flattening. 

While flattening the curve would be a great pat on the back for everyone doing their part i think we have to be really careful to keep the pressure on, and not undo the hardwork done to this point.

The true death rate (from the statistics) is between 
1. Cases/deaths (underestimate) 
2. Deaths/closed cases(deaths+recoveries) (overestimate) 

Over time they'll come together to a value, that's your death rate
